reader_summary: I understand the debugging problem as locating whether an assistant got the user’s words wrong or answered those words badly. The correct source transcript bypasses ASR to test the chat stage; actual recognition output tests the whole voice route. Both routes must use the same question requirements, history, photo and chat weights. Losing 不 turns a request for a non-spicy dinner into a request that lacks that restriction. The short program compares two hand-written strings, not recordings or generated answers. It reports one change among nine reference characters, 11.1%, and unequal strings; restoring 不 produces zero and equal strings. A small spelling difference can still change the intention entirely. I understand why the original ASR transcript must be preserved even when a user corrects it, and why read-aloud questions do not cover spontaneous conversation. However, I had to infer the fraction underlying CER from the reported numbers, and the allowed edit operations are not explained, so I cannot explain the general metric confidently from the provided reading.
